{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"326aa0f2a6d23920a3fc0a0075c800eb51f655014633d8bd0f4807b7622d9f09","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road: pedestrians, the Safe Passing Law, motorcycles, trucks and buses, mopeds, bicycles and scooters, trains, off-road vehicles, animals and horses","heading":"C — Sharing the road: pedestrian right-of-way and speed, turning near pedestrians, the Safe Passing Law, motorcycles, truck and bus no-zones, yielding to buses, mopeds, bicycles, skateboards and inline skates, motorized scooters and low-speed vehicles, trains, off-road vehicles, animals and horses","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Sharing the road: pedestrian right-of-way and speed, turning near pedestrians, the Safe Passing Law, motorcycles, truck and bus no-zones, yielding to buses, mopeds, bicycles, skateboards and inline skates, motorized scooters and low-speed vehicles, trains, off-road vehicles, animals and horses
Knowledge domain: how a New Jersey driver protects the road users who are easiest to hurt or hardest to see — pedestrians, cyclists, skaters, motorcyclists, moped and scooter riders and horseback riders — and how to stay out of trouble around trucks, buses and trains.

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Pedestrian safety is shared, but drivers carry the primary duty to prevent crashes with pedestrians, who are the most vulnerable road users. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0146]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian struck by a car at 20 mph has about a five percent chance of dying, but at 40 mph that rate jumps to 85 percent. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0146]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Every corner of an intersection has a crosswalk even when no lines are painted, and this is called an unmarked crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0146]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Drivers must stop and stay stopped for a pedestrian in a marked crosswalk, and yield to a pedestrian crossing in an unmarked one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0146]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
If the signal changes from WALK to DON'T WALK while a pedestrian is crossing, the driver must still stop, and a driver may never block or park in a crosswalk or pass a vehicle stopped at one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0146]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop for a pedestrian can mean fines, possible jail, community service, points and license suspension, with tougher penalties if serious bodily injury results. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A02
On a road with several lanes, stop well short of the crosswalk so you do not hide the pedestrian from drivers in the next lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A02
Pedestrians must obey signals and may not step suddenly into the path of a car too close to yield, but their mistakes never excuse a driver from using due care. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A02
Slow down in school zones and near bus stops, playgrounds, parks and business districts, and watch around parked vehicles where pedestrians, especially children, may appear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A02
Before any turn, and especially a right on red, scan left, right and behind, check mirrors and blind spots, and look for pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A03
Under the Safe Passing Law, move over one lane when you can, leave at least four feet when passing on a single-lane road, and if four feet is impossible slow to 25 mph and be ready to stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A03
Laws for cars and trucks also apply to motorcycles, but a rider may react differently, so check blind spots twice before changing lanes or turning. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A03
Never follow a motorcycle too closely, because it may be able to stop in a shorter distance than other vehicles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A04
When a motorcycle passes you, keep your speed and position and give it room to finish the pass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A04
The most common cause of motorcycle crashes is a driver failing to notice and recognize the motorcycle in traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A04
In bad weather a truck, tractor-trailer or bus may need as much as 25 percent longer to stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A04
When a truck or bus driver cannot see your vehicle in their rearview or side mirrors, your vehicle is sitting in a no-zone, or blind spot. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A05
Stay well back from a truck that is getting ready to back up or is backing, and never pass close behind it, because the area behind it is a blind spot for everyone. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0150]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A06
Hang farther back than usual behind a large truck or bus so that you show up in its driver's mirrors, and never get sandwiched between large vehicles. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A06
When stopped behind a large vehicle at a light or sign, leave room, especially facing uphill, because it may roll back slightly as it starts. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A06
A truck may need to swing wide to the left to make a right turn, so give it extra road space. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A06
After passing a truck, do not pull back in front until you can see its entire front in your rearview mirror, and never pass a truck on the right. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A07
Do not linger in the long blind spots along a truck's sides, and bear right when a large vehicle comes toward you to reduce wind turbulence and the risk of a sideswipe. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A07
All non-emergency vehicles must yield to a bus re-entering traffic after picking up or dropping off passengers, and violators face a $50 to $200 fine, up to 15 days in jail, or both. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A07
Mopeds are low-speed two-wheelers with pedals that may not go faster than 25 mph and must ride on the right with the flow of traffic. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A07
Bicyclists, skateboarders and inline skaters have the same rights and duties as motor vehicles, and New Jersey classes them as vulnerable road users. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A08
Breaking the Safe Passing Law and causing bodily injury brings a $500 fine and 2 points, while a violation without injury brings a $100 fine and no points. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0153]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A08
A bicycle ridden after dark must have front and rear lights and a rear reflector, though these can still be hard for drivers to see. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0153]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A08
A driver signaling a right turn must yield to bicyclists, skateboarders and inline skaters going through the intersection. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0153]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A08
Riding a motorized scooter on public roads or sidewalks is illegal, with the only exception being designated municipal or county property. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0153]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A09
A motorized scooter must be registered where the owner lives and insured, and no one under 12, or the local minimum age, may operate one. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0154]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A10
A freight train going 55 mph can need a mile or more to stop, and trains always have the right of way. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0155]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A10
Only enter a railroad crossing when there is room to clear the tracks completely on the far side, since a train can stick out three feet or more beyond the rails on each side. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0155]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A10
Do not pass other vehicles within 100 feet of a railroad crossing, and do not shift gears on the tracks in a manual transmission vehicle. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0155]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A12
When approaching or passing someone riding a horse or driving a horse-drawn vehicle, slow to 25 mph or less and go carefully. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0157]

Misconceptions: an unpainted corner is still a crosswalk; a pedestrian's mistake does not cancel the driver's duty of care; motorcycles can stop faster than cars, so tailgating one is dangerous; seeing a truck does not mean its driver sees you; a train looks farther away and slower than it really is.
Mnemonics: four feet or slow to twenty-five for the Safe Passing Law; five percent at twenty but eighty-five percent at forty for pedestrian deaths; a car the truck driver cannot see in the mirrors is in a no-zone; a mile or more for a freight train to stop.
Glossary: unmarked crosswalk means the legal crossing at an intersection corner with no painted lines; vulnerable road user means a pedestrian, cyclist, skater or similar user who is easily hurt; no-zone means a blind spot around a truck or bus; moped means a low-speed pedal-equipped motorized bicycle; low-speed vehicle means a small four-wheeled vehicle with a capped top speed.
Dynamic facts: fines, minimum ages set by local governments and the moped and motorcycle safety web pages can change; confirm them on official New Jersey websites.
